description: Modular Testbed Building (MTB2): A Shared-Use, Reconfigurable, Earthquake-Resistant Design is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Joel Conte, University of California San Diego (ucsd.edu). This project aims to verify the structural behavioral predictions of computer algorithms. In addition, it seeks to prove the importance of modular structural design in earthquake-prone regions. The data in this project can be reused to develop future experiments using the modular testbed building. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-rm7v-fe30. Keywords: resilient, reusable, buckling-restrained braces, DuraFuse plates, stretch length anchors. Published 2021-08-25. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
